title: Classify edge-matching equality and sharp odd-difference image maxima (no κ)
body:
**The irreducible edge-matching image bound has a parity restriction, and the exact maximum is now known whenever k−nu is odd.** For binary rank-one idempotents with nonzero off-patterns, k is the pattern dimension, nu is the matrix-unit graph's maximum matching size, and n is the joint-image dimension.

- If `k−nu = 1 modulo 4`, the sharp maximum is `n=(3k+nu−1)/2`.
- If `k−nu = 3 modulo 4`, the sharp maximum is `n=(3k+nu−3)/2`.

Read the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2523029b27d40526b811591ce0fb85f9bc1b1df7/research/edge-matching-equality-classification/PROOF.md), [receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2523029b27d40526b811591ce0fb85f9bc1b1df7/research/edge-matching-equality-classification/RESULT.json), [finite exceptional certificates](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2523029b27d40526b811591ce0fb85f9bc1b1df7/research/edge-matching-equality-classification/EXCEPTIONS.json) and [checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2523029b27d40526b811591ce0fb85f9bc1b1df7/research/edge-matching-equality-classification/verify.py). These are all-dimension results with two explicit finite proof steps after reduction to widths three and four.

Every pool attaining `2n=3k+nu−1` is classified: nu disjoint unit pairs, an even number `(k−nu−1)/2` of normal triples and one fresh link, with the one-dimensional case stated separately. It has exactly n projectors and odd n. The classification treats the complete pool, including extra lifts; it does not assume an irreducible image-basis subcollection. A second construction attains the improved bound for the other odd residue class. The even-difference maximum and classification of the lower attainers remain open.

**No new kappa**, paid word, G20 provider, native realization or complete invoice is supplied. Coordinate projectors are excluded. The selected frontier and all five assumptions remain. The existing orthogonal-basis single-bridge word obstruction still applies where its relation-lattice premises hold. This completes the [advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19708785).

Normal and optimized CPython 3.12.16 checks pass on macOS arm64. The finite reduction enumerates all 868 unordered invertible bases at widths three and four. All 357 qualifying complete pools have a retained proper invariant subspace. Raw rank-one scans and separate pattern lifting agree; every nonzero-vector orbit is also checked. The normal-triple lemma is rechecked. All 23133 nonzero patterns of 37 attaining fixtures are lifted. Another 1050 links in two column-triple domains check the complete-pool covector obstruction, including pools with extra members. Odd-triple trace/kernel controls and an irreducible even-image control show the theorem's boundaries.

Metadata, source history, committed bytes, modes, export, archive integrity and read-only optimized replay without Git or a usable PATH pass. With CPython 3.12 and its standard library, from the repository root:

```sh
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/edge-matching-equality-classification/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/edge-matching-equality-classification
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/edge-matching-equality-classification --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Expected markers:

```text
PASS_EDGE_MATCHING_EQUALITY_CLASSIFICATION
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE
PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES
```

Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44308389120/job/134815812059) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence. Selected cold replay, full predecessor package replays, native, Lean and Docker checks were not run. Independent human and formal-kernel review are unclaimed. The unrestricted conclusion uses the written support argument and the explicitly complete finite exceptional certificates, not extrapolation from examples.

Prepared by @aliromman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. The consumed matching and disjoint-relation theorem is Ali Romman's [PR #7692](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7692), [pinned proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c2870a38841f515db7203a0761cd77f014f7fb7a/research/edge-matching-image-bound/PROOF.md). Its binary pool and orbit primitives are adapted. The complete-coset argument extends [PR #7691](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7691), [pinned seven-image proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/69e70b1426c32b19da8334930815800a2c95ffca/research/no-edge-dim5-extremal-classification/PROOF.md). The exceptional lower construction uses the three-copy pool lemma of [PR #7688](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7688), [pinned proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d9aba79eaed566640353efcb0a27b0d5649f705a/research/no-edge-basis-extraction-failure/PROOF.md).

The all-pair endpoint in [PR #7693](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7693) and the two-triple endpoint in [PR #7691](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7691) remain prior classifications. The relevant word obstruction is [PR #7695](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7695), [pinned proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/996c002d82420141c19797e4e3b699ed88aee330/research/orthogonal-basis-bridge-obstruction/PROOF.md). [Credit details](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2523029b27d40526b811591ce0fb85f9bc1b1df7/research/edge-matching-equality-classification/CREDITS.md) preserve the matrix-unit fiber, normal-triple and fresh-link results of Jerry Chen (@CubeJerry), Nick Petalas (@petalas) and @unpaidmoon. Those blocks and special cases are not newly claimed. New work is Apache-2.0.
